correctness.rationale: The q=2 source/sink/interior response classification is complete above length four. At q=3, the seven pointed cases determined by distance 0,1,2 from either endpoint versus a three-deep interior give a winning two-round continuation for lengths at least eight, while an exact game check gives Spoiler a win on lengths 7 and 8. For q>=4, Brown--Hoshino's protected-gap strategy is orientation-preserving when the same signed displacement and corresponding endpoint side are copied. The undirected lower bound transfers through \(E=S\lor S^{-1}\), except the directed q=3 boundary that is handled separately. A fresh independent exact EF solver reproduced every case for \(1\le q\le3\), \(1\le n\le m\le10\), including \(P_7\not\equiv_3P_8\).

value.rationale: The result identifies the exact effect of orientation on a canonical finite-model family: it changes precisely the rank-three cutoff while leaving the higher dyadic regime intact. Exact quantifier-rank thresholds are natural benchmarks for finite-variable distinguishability, and the P7/P8 boundary is structurally motivated rather than an arbitrary finite case.

final_claim: For finite nonempty successor paths \(\vec P_n\), \(\vec P_n\equiv_q\vec P_m\) exactly when \(q\le1\), or \(n=m\), or \(q\ge2\) and both lengths are at least \(2^q\); hence unequal lengths \(n<m\) first separate at rank \(\max\{2,\lfloor\log_2n\rfloor+1\}\).
limitations: Single consistently oriented paths in the language with equality and successor only.
No linear order predicate, endpoint constants, counting logic, arbitrary orientations, or unions.
